I don’t think it’s exactly like that for me.\n\nDoctor: During those moments when you freeze, do you feel detached from yourself or like the situation around you isn’t quite real?\n\nPatient: I’m… not sure. I don’t think I’m floating outside myself or anything like that. It’s more like I lose the thread, like when you walk into the walk-in cooler and forget why you’re there, except everyone can see it happening.\n\nThe room is still the room, I think. The soda station is still sticky and the ice machine is still making that grinding noise—our ice machine has been weird for months, actually, and the repair guy always comes during lunch rush, which is ridiculous. But… yeah, I don’t know about “not real.” I haven’t really noticed it that way.\n\nDoctor: When this happens, do you feel confused?\n\nPatient: Yeah… confused, I guess. Not like I don’t know where I am, but I stop doing the thing I’m supposed to be doing. Like at work I’ll be in the middle of service and suddenly I’m just standing by the soda station with the cash drawer key in my hand, saying table numbers over and over instead of closing out checks.\n\nThat’s what scared people, I think. Because it’s dinner rush and everyone needs something, and I’m doing it all wrong or not in the right order. Then someone has to tell me, like, “You were supposed to cash out table 9,” and I’m still thinking about table 12 or 14 or whichever one.\n\nDoctor: Have you had any recent head injury, seizure, fever, or new drug or medication use?\n\nPatient: I don’t think so… I mean, I haven’t, like, hit my head or anything that I remember. No one’s said I had a seizure. Fever, I don’t know—I don’t really check unless I feel really awful, and I’ve been going to work because if you call out they act like the whole restaurant is going to collapse, even though people call out all the time.\n\nNew drugs or medicine… no, not that I can think of. Like I’ll look over and they’re just doing whatever they were doing, and then I feel stupid because I already said, “What?” out loud.\n\nDoctor: When you hear the woman’s voice say your name, does it sound like it’s coming from outside you, as if someone in the room is speaking?\n\nPatient: Yeah… I mean, it sounds like it’s in the room, I guess. The work ones bother me more because we’re counting and everyone’s already tense about the drawer being off by like two dollars, and then I hear this woman saying I’m doing the count wrong. But then I look around and nobody’s reacting, like no one heard anything, so… I don’t know.
